subject: [URGENT] Production impact after v2alpha model deploy - request for rollback
messages:
From: Nicolas Dupont <nicolas.dupont@tradeflow.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@tradeflow.com
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected latency & errors after v2alpha rollout

Hi Naomi,

We pushed the v2alpha model and the new INT8 quant profile in our canary rings this morning (2027-03-14 08:45 PDT). Almost immediately we saw an increase in end-to-end p95 from ~340ms to ~1.1s and a spike in 5xx errors (service timeouts + decode errors) — error rate climbed to ~2.6% on traffic to the new variant. Throughput for high-concurrency paths dropped by ~30% (seen in our gateway metrics).

Examples: request ids tf-7b2a1, tf-7b2a6, tf-7b2b0 (attached samples and traces). Customers are hitting timeouts in the acceptance region and our ops team is getting paging alerts.

We need immediate help: can Redwood confirm whether the v2alpha quant profile is known to cause kernel thrashing on A100s or if there's a serving configuration we missed? TradeFlow would like rollback to the previous variant if rollback is safe and can be executed quickly — we are also open to a temporary capacity bump but need guidance.

Please escalate to engineering if needed; this is impacting our live traffic.

Thanks,
Nicolas
Principal SRE, TradeFlow Capital

Attachments: tradeflow-error-samples.jsonl (5KB), p95_p99_traces-20270314.png (120KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Nicolas Dupont <nicolas.dupont@tradeflow.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & errors after v2alpha rollout

Hi Nicolas — thank you for the quick heads-up and the samples. We've pulled the traces and I’m escalating to infra and model ops now.

Immediate plan (short term):
- Acknowledge and collect: Marcus will triage kernel/runtime signals and confirm whether the quant profile is the likely root cause.
- Containment: If rollback is straightforward we can schedule a short rollback window; please confirm approximate traffic % on the v2alpha ring (canary vs prod).
- Communication: I’ll coordinate timing and get back with a concrete rollback ETA and a proposed customer-facing message.

Please expect a follow-up in ~30–45 minutes. Looping in the on-call infra and product ops.

—Naomi

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & errors after v2alpha rollout

Naomi / team — initial triage from runtime metrics and kernel logs:
- Observed: sustained increase in GPU kernel preemption and scheduling spikes coincident with requests hitting the v2alpha INT8 variant. p99 decoding stalls and >20% longer memcpy times in the critical path.
- Likely cause: the v2alpha quant profile reduces token-width tiling which increases kernel launch count for short sequences; on our A100 fleet this seems to cause contention between decode and KV cache rebuild paths.
- Temporary mitigations: 1) Pin the model to FP16 variant for the canary ring (model_id: tradeflow-v1.9-fp16), 2) increase decode threads and bump per-instance batch concurrency to reduce per-request kernel overhead.

Rollback notes (safe path):
- We can perform a model-variant rollback via the console. Steps in rollback-playbook-steps.md. Expected customer-facing impact: ~30–45 minutes of redeploy/regeneration of warmed caches; short-term p95 should return to baseline within ~60 minutes post-rollback.
- Risk: KV cache invalidation could cause a transient latency bump for warmups; we should schedule during a low-traffic window and coordinate connection draining.

Recommend: Immediate rollback to tradeflow-v1.9-fp16. I’ll prepare a one-click change with a fast failback plan if rollback doesn't reduce errors.

—Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback-playbook-steps.md

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & errors after v2alpha rollout

Team — operational notes and proposed schedule:
- TradeFlow canary currently ~12% of traffic (confirmed with Nicolas).
- Proposed rollback window: 2027-03-14 23:30–00:30 UTC (PDT evening), target to finish within 45 minutes.
- Pre-rollback checklist: notify TradeFlow ops, take a snapshot of canary metrics, set temporary alert thresholds for p50/p95/p99, prepare capacity bump if needed.
- Post-rollback: monitor p99 and error traces for 2 hours; open a postmortem doc and preserve logs.

I’ll draft the customer-facing note once Naomi confirms timing. Rishi — inventory of contractual credits?

—Grace

Nicolas — we’ve scheduled the rollback to the FP16 variant tonight at 23:30 UTC (2027-03-14) with a target completion of 00:15–00:30 UTC. Summary:
- Action: rollback to tradeflow-v1.9-fp16 across canary ring; internal infra will also bump concurrency and monitor kernel preemption signals.
- Expected impact: short cache warmup latencies (~1–2 minutes) and temporary elevated p99 as caches repopulate; overall p95/p99 should return to baseline within 60 minutes.
- Post-rollback: Redwood will provide a short postmortem and a set of config recommendations to safely redeploy v2alpha once we harden the quant profile.
- Credits: Rishi will follow up on any commercial remediation — we’ll propose a one-month service credit if the rollback and follow-up remediation does not meet your acceptance criteria.

We’ll send a one-line status update at start and confirm when complete. Thanks for flagging this early — apologies for the disruption.

—Naomi Feldman
